title: SLA Licensing & Outdoor Dining Committee
one_line: The SLA committee heard liquor-license applications, voted yes on three of them, and was still reading stipulations when the digest ends.

segments.label: Call to order
segments.summary: Clint Smeltzer opened the April 13 SLA committee with attendance and the agenda. No items had been withdrawn, so everything on the agenda was to be heard. A few shorter items were taken first, out of order.
facts: Withdrawals
The chair said no items had withdrawn and every agenda item would be heard.
Order
A few shorter items were taken out of order before the rest of the agenda.
Attendance
Megan Joy and Stephen Ballinger were present. Michael Lavario was marked absent at the start and later voted.

segments.label: Outdoor dining notice
segments.summary: During the first application, Susan asked restaurants to attend a Zoom on outdoor dining regulations. She said the meeting was Wednesday afternoon from 2 to 4 and that she could send the registration link. She said the comment was not about that applicant's file.
facts: Zoom
Susan announced a Wednesday Zoom from 2 to 4 p.m. for restaurants on outdoor dining regulations.
Invite
She asked people to attend and said she could send the registration link.
followups: Send the registration link for the Wednesday outdoor dining Zoom.

segments.label: License applications
segments.outcome: Voted on three applications; the digest has no tally for the others.
segments.summary: The committee heard a partner change, a full-license matter first approved in June 2025, hour changes, and new or upgraded licenses. It voted yes on a bar and tavern at 50 Avenue B, on beer-and-wine stipulations at 40 Avenue B, and on basement seats at 94 Avenue. The night included additional applications, including a quick stipulation change with a 10 p.m. close whose tally is not shown. Cynthia NYC was called, and the digest ends while stipulations are being read for 349 East 13th Street.
facts: Partner change
The remaining partner, Pierre, keeps the same stipulations. Only the partnership changes. The digest does not show a vote.
June 2025 license
The chair said a full liquor license was approved about a year earlier, with a caveat after the SLA found a nearby church was a full-service church. This night's vote is not in the digest.
412 and 414 East 9th Street
Method-of-operation change for a seafood restaurant. Hours were read as Monday through Saturday 5 p.m. to midnight and Sunday noon to midnight, with other stipulations unchanged. No vote is shown.
50 Avenue B

Full liquor license for a bar and tavern. A block association that had opposed it resolved its issues, and resident stipulations including soundproofing were added. Hours discussed were noon to 2 a.m. The committee voted yes.
40 Avenue B

The applicant sought a full license where the location had beer and wine. The East Village Community Coalition opposed the upgrade. The committee voted yes on beer-and-wine stipulations, 2 p.m. to midnight, no licensed security, and no class change to a full license without returning to the community board.
94 Avenue

Elizabeth McGrath's operating restaurant asked to add a basement with nine tables and 19 seats. Other stipulations stayed the same, including a full license, hours of 11 a.m. to 4 a.m., and no outdoor space. The committee voted yes.
32 East First Street
Cynthia NYC was called with the applicant and Bruno present. The digest does not include a recommendation or vote.
349 East 13th Street

Jimmy Leather Pants LLC was read as a full-license Idaho-themed restaurant with acoustic live music and no DJs. Hours read were Sunday noon to midnight, Monday through Thursday noon to 2 a.m., and Friday and Saturday noon to 4 a.m. The digest ends before a vote.
followups: Send the written stipulation for the 94 Avenue basement alteration.
Return to the community board before seeking a full on-premises license.
Install soundproofing so sound is not audible in nearby apartments.
